title: Saudi Arabia wants a car industry, launches Ceer with two EVs
gist: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and Foxconn have launched Ceer, the Kingdom's first domestic automaker, unveiling the flagship Exobot sedan and SUV (112 kWh battery, 1,111 hp, ~300-400 mile real-world range, steer-by-wire yoke) as part of Vision 2030 economic diversification, with plans for seven models and 35,000 jobs by 2030/2034, though success hinges on unproven mainstream affordability against dominant Chinese brands.

insights.claim: Ceer is a joint venture between Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and Foxconn, and is the Kingdom's first-ever domestic automaker, positioned as a core part of Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 plan to diversify the economy away from oil and build local technological/industrial capability by the end of the decade.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: Unlike Lucid (in which PIF is merely an investor), PIF directly owns Ceer, giving Saudi Arabia full strategic control over a sovereign automotive industry play, relevant for tracking PIF's shift from passive foreign EV investment to building domestic industrial capacity.
insights.locator: A joint venture between the country's Public Investment Fund and Foxconn

insights.claim: Ceer plans to have seven vehicles in its portfolio by 2030, some of which will be hybrids, and currently has no plans to sell outside the GCC region, though the company says expansion is possible if demand exists; the vehicles were designed from the start to be quickly homologated for global markets including Europe and possibly North America.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: A seven-model roadmap with built-in global homologation optionality signals Ceer could become an export competitor beyond the Gulf if its mainstream (non-flagship) models prove commercially viable, a name to watch in global EV market-share dynamics.
insights.locator: It plans to have seven new cars in its portfolio by 2030

insights.claim: As part of Vision 2030, Saudi Arabia is promoting a 'Saudi Made' local-manufacturing branding initiative across many consumer products, and Ceer gives the Kingdom a fully domestic automotive alternative to established brands (including Lucid) that directly supports local manufacturing and the economy.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: The 'Saudi Made' push could create preferential domestic demand for Ceer over imported and even PIF-linked foreign brands like Lucid, a potential headwind for non-domestic automakers' Saudi market share.
insights.locator: as part of the Vision 2030 plan, Saudi Arabia is encouraging

insights.claim: In the US, every one automotive manufacturing job is estimated to create five additional jobs in the local economy via suppliers and related support systems; Ceer projects 35,000 direct and indirect jobs by 2034 from its dedicated manufacturing complex near Jeddah.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: The jobs multiplier framing signals Saudi Arabia is using Ceer as an economic-diversification anchor project, not just a product launch, relevant to assessing Vision 2030's broader industrial-policy credibility.
insights.locator: If all goes to plan, Ceer expects 35,000 direct and indirect jobs

insights.claim: The launch Exobot models feature a 112-kWh battery pack delivering over 310 miles (500 km) NEDC range for the SUV and at least 373 miles (600 km) NEDC for the sedan, with a real-world estimate of 300-400 miles putting them on par with the latest BMW and Mercedes EV platforms; the vehicles use an 800V architecture with a DC fast-charge time of roughly 30 minutes to 80%, comparable to the Kia EV9 and Hyundai Ioniq 9.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: Range and charging specs competitive with premium German EV platforms suggest Ceer's flagship is a credible technical entrant, not just a symbolic vanity project, worth benchmarking against Western/Chinese premium EV competitors.
insights.locator: The launch model Exobots will have a 112-kWh battery pack

insights.claim: The Exobot delivers 1,111 hp (828 kW) and 1,100 lb-ft (1,500 Nm) of torque via a tri-motor setup with torque vectoring, reaching 0-62 mph in just over 2 seconds for the sedan and 2.4 seconds for the SUV, with a quarter-mile time of 10 seconds, using steer-by-wire technology (including a yoke) enabled by the 800V system.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: These performance figures place the Exobot in the same class as top-tier performance EVs (e.g., Lucid Air Sapphire, Tesla Plaid), signaling Ceer is targeting the premium/halo segment to establish brand credibility before scaling to mainstream, more affordable models.
insights.locator: Performance is the main goal of these vehicles

insights.claim: Ceer CTO Markus Leitner argues the company's differentiation isn't novel individual hardware (triple motors, torque vectoring, air suspension are now industry-standard) but superior systems integration of these components to optimize the driving experience.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: This is a notably modest competitive claim (integration, not innovation) for a from-scratch automaker, suggesting Ceer's near-term strategy leans on execution quality rather than proprietary technology breakthroughs — a useful lens for assessing its defensibility versus established OEMs.
insights.quote: Everyone has triple motors. Everyone has torque vectoring. Everyone has air suspension. What we do better than anyone else is integrate that all together to provide the best driving experience.

insights.claim: Ceer confirmed Apple CarPlay and Android Auto will be available at launch, its infotainment system is proprietary IP co-developed with Foxconn and other partners, and over-the-air updates will be available that can improve any vehicle aspect including performance and range.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: OTA-upgradeable performance and standard smartphone integration signal Ceer is following the Tesla/Rivian software-defined-vehicle playbook rather than a traditional hardware-only automaker model.
insights.locator: In an interview with Ars Technica, Chief Technology Officer Markus Leitner confirmed

insights.claim: Ceer CEO James Deluca has extensive manufacturing experience from General Motors and also spent time at VinFast, whose rapid pivot from building gasoline cars to EVs happened 'lightning-quick' even though VinFast itself did not take off in the US market; much of Ceer's leadership team has backgrounds at GM, Magna Steyr, or other established legacy automakers.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: A leadership team with legacy-automaker manufacturing depth plus VinFast's speed-to-market experience is a credibility signal for Ceer's ability to execute a fast, seven-model rollout by 2030, though VinFast's own US market struggles are a cautionary parallel.
insights.locator: Deluca spent a lot of time at General Motors in manufacturing

insights.claim: The author frames Ceer's ultimate success or failure ('will this be successful or will it be the next Fisker?') as hinging not on the aspirational flagship Exobot models but on the upcoming more mainstream models' affordability and competitiveness against Chinese brands, which currently dominate Saudi Arabia's auto market.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: The real investment/commercial test for Ceer is its future mass-market EV pricing and quality versus entrenched Chinese automakers in Saudi Arabia, not the current halo-product reveal — a key metric to track over the next several product launches.
insights.locator: Will this be successful or will it be the next Fisker?

insights.claim: Despite significant capital backing from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, the article notes Ceer's flagship doors (falcon-style 'Shahin Wing' doors) face an unresolved engineering test from the region's extreme climate, and the author is 'surprised' if such doors appear on any future, more mainstream Ceer models.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: Flagship-specific design flourishes not expected to carry to mainstream models suggest Ceer is using the Exobot primarily as a brand-building halo product rather than a template for its volume vehicles.
insights.locator: Not having a B-pillar makes access to the second row much easier
